statements.t: The company continues to expect positive volume trends and increasing benefits from its ongoing operational improvement efforts.

While the company has made strong progress on the planned actions to optimize its production network, these benefits are not expected to fully offset the near-term impact of higher input costs and weaker end market demand.
At the same time, several working capital initiatives are anticipated to generate additional cash flow, supporting the company's ability to maintain its operating cash flow guidance.
In the meantime, our working capital initiatives continue to generate cash, allowing us to maintain our operating cash flow guidance and raise our free cash flow outlook.”
Presentation materials will be available at least 15 minutes before the call on www.koppers.com in the Investor Relations section of the company’s website.

Our team of approximately 1,700 employees create, protect and preserve key elements of our global infrastructure – including railroad crossties, utility poles, outdoor wooden structures, and production feedstocks for steel, aluminum and construction materials, among others – applying decades of industry-leading expertise while constantly innovating to anticipate the needs of tomorrow.

statements.t: We believe this will grow earnings per share, lower our maintenance and capital requirements and consistently generate higher margins.
We expect the crosstie market to remain stable and within this range.
• Product demand for our PC business has historically been associated with consumer spending on home repair and remodeling projects in North America.
Our PC business expects higher volumes through market share growth and acquiring new customers, including international expansion.
We have invested in projects to increase distillation yields and balance raw material supply and cost with customer demand and pricing.

Our outlook reflects plans to substantially offset costs related to import and export tariffs, where possible, but there is continued uncertainty regarding the implementation dates and scope of potential additional tariffs, as well as potential retaliatory trade policy.
As a result of these items, our outlook may vary.
As a result of the foregoing, we anticipate that we may experience material fluctuations in quarterly operating results.
We anticipate that our liquidity will continue to be adequate to fund our cash requirements for at least the next twelve months.
